newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congressmen propose end to Cuba food embargo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressmen propose end to Cuba food embargo.

text.p: A bipartisan group of members of Congress on Wednesday announced they would introduce legislation calling for an end to the embargo on food and medicine to Cuba.

The group of 12 lawmakers, including House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach, Republican from Iowa, and Charles Rangel, Democrat of New York, said free trade with Cuba of food and medicine was an important way to end hunger, low-birth weight of newborns and medical problems of the elderly in Cuba.

At a news conference, Rangel and other lawmakers said the current debate about China and its Most Favored Nation trading status underscored the need to open trade links with the 11 million people living under the communist government of Fidel Castro.
"Here we are dealing with more than one billion communists," Rangel said, "when we have a beautiful group of people living in the Caribbean who are our neighbors."
"I truly believe this is a moral issues, not a political issue," Rangel added.
A variety of medical studies have shown that since Cuba's relationship with the former Soviet Union collapsed, many Cubans do not get enough to eat or access to medicine.

The planned legislation is certain to encounter opposition from Florida's congressional delegation and from Sen. Jesse Helms, Republican of South Carolina, who co-authored the Helms-Burton act to tighten the U.S. embargo against Cuba.
